True effects of a simulation design

Source: R/simulate.R
biscal_truth.Rd

Computes the true separable and total treatment effects of a simulation design with a single standard normal covariate (such as the designs of the paper), either at given covariate values or averaged over the covariate distribution, the targets of aste() and easte(). Population-level values are computed by numerical integration.

Usage

biscal_truth(K = 20, case = 1, coefs = NULL, y1 = 0, y2 = 0, x = NULL)

Arguments

K

End time point.

case, coefs

The design, as in simulate_biscal().

y1, y2

Thresholds of the generalized odds ratio, as codes 0, 1, ... of the response categories (not the highest).

x

Optional numeric vector of covariate values. If NULL (default), population-level values under \(X \sim N(0, 1)\) are returned.

Value

With x = NULL, a named vector with the true ESTE1, ESTE2, ETTE, EASTE1, EASTE2 and DEASTE. Otherwise a data frame with the true STE1, STE2, TTE, ASTE1, ASTE2 and DASTE at each value of x.

References

Hu, P. and Yi, G. Y. (2026). Inference about separable causal effects with longitudinal bivariate ordinal responses with missingness and censoring. Statistics in Medicine, 45, e70320. doi:10.1002/sim.70320

See also

simulate_biscal(), biscal_coefs().

Examples

# true DEASTE of the three cases (Table 5 of the paper)
sapply(1:3, function(case) biscal_truth(K = 20, case = case)[["DEASTE"]])
#> [1]  0.006515171  0.000000000 -0.093659166
biscal_truth(K = 20, case = 1, x = c(-1, 0, 1))
#>    x         STE1         STE2          TTE       ASTE1       ASTE2       DASTE
#> 1 -1 -0.013793451 -0.002554046 -0.008173749 0.013793451 0.002554046 0.011239405
#> 2  0 -0.010164266 -0.003870253 -0.007017260 0.010164266 0.003870253 0.006294012
#> 3  1 -0.006131398 -0.004093514 -0.005112456 0.006131398 0.004093514 0.002037885
